Description: Use semantic color names with foreground pattern

Dark mode overrides the same semantic tokens inside a .dark selector. In the Tailwind v4 setup, tokens hold full color values (the default theme converted HSL to OKLCH) and are mapped to utilities with @theme inline; the v3-era pattern of bare HSL channels wrapped as hsl(var(--token)) no longer applies.
Do: Define each token in :root and .dark with full color values and map them with @theme inline
Don't: Bare HSL channel triplets consumed through hsl(var(--token)) in a Tailwind v4 project
Code Good: :root { --background: /* full color value */; } .dark { --background: /* full color value */; } @theme inline { --color-background: var(--background); }
Code Bad: --color-background: hsl(var(--background)); /* v3-era wrapper around bare HSL channels */

Guideline: Build forms with Field and your form library
Description: The forms docs build fields from <Field />, <FieldLabel />, <FieldDescription /> and <FieldError />, wired to React Hook Form through its <Controller /> (a TanStack Form guide also exists). The older Form/FormField wrapper is no longer what the docs teach.
Do: Controller render prop returning Field + FieldLabel + control + FieldError
Don't: Start new forms on the older Form/FormField/FormItem wrapper
Code Good: <Controller name="title" control={form.control} render={({ field, fieldState }) => (<Field data-invalid={fieldState.invalid}><FieldLabel htmlFor={field.name}>Title</FieldLabel><Input {...field} id={field.name} aria-invalid={fieldState.invalid} />{fieldState.invalid && <FieldError errors={[fieldState.error]} />}</Field>)} />

Guideline: Expose invalid state on the field and the control
Description: Set data-invalid on <Field /> and aria-invalid on the control, and render <FieldError /> with the validation errors, so styling and assistive technology both see the invalid state.
Do: data-invalid on Field, aria-invalid on the input, FieldError for messages
Don't: Error text without aria-invalid on the control

Description: Define form schema with Zod for type-safe validation
shadcn ships both Select, a custom popup listbox, and NativeSelect, a styled native HTML <select>. Pick by the interaction you need; a native select is a supported option, not an anti-pattern.
Do: NativeSelect when native select behavior fits; Select when you need the custom listbox
Don't: Rebuild a select from divs, or rule out the native element by default
Code Bad:
Choose…

Guideline: Compose with asChild (Radix) or render (Base UI)
Description: shadcn components are built on Radix or Base UI depending on the project's chosen base, and composition differs. Radix components take asChild; Base UI components take a render prop. For links styled as buttons with Base UI, the docs say to use buttonVariants on a plain <a>, because Button keeps role="button".
Do: Check the component source; use asChild on Radix, render or buttonVariants on Base UI
Don't: Pass asChild to Base UI components or nest an <a> inside <Button>
Code Good: <Button asChild><Link href="/">Home</Link></Button> // Radix  —  <Link href="/" className={buttonVariants()}>Home</Link> // Base UI link
